script = '''import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace")

import os
import email
from email.mime.text import MIMEText

TESTBED = "/workspace/testbed"

# Email content
sender = "alice"
recipient = "ethan"
subject = "Follow-Up: High-Priority Onboarding Equipment Setup Request"
body = """Dear Ethan,

I am writing to follow up on the high-priority onboarding equipment setup request. As outlined in the original request, the following items are needed for the new team member before the next business day:

1. Windows Laptop - Provisioned and configured with all standard company software and security policies.
2. VPN Access - Full remote-access VPN credentials and client setup to ensure secure connectivity from day one.
3. Email Configuration - Corporate email account created, configured, and tested on the assigned device.

Given the high-priority nature of this request and the tight turnaround, could you please provide a status update on each item at your earliest convenience? If there are any blockers or additional information needed to expedite the process, please do not hesitate to let me know.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Best regards,
Alice"""

# Build the .eml content
msg = MIMEText(body)
msg["From"] = f"{sender}@example.com"
msg["To"] = f"{recipient}@example.com"
msg["Subject"] = subject

eml_content = msg.as_string()
eml_filename = f"{subject}.eml"

# Ensure recipient and sender directories exist
for user in [sender, recipient]:
    user_dir = os.path.join(TESTBED, "emails", user)
    os.makedirs(user_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Write to recipient inbox
recipient_path = os.path.join(TESTBED, "emails", recipient, eml_filename)
with open(recipient_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(eml_content)
print(f"SENT: Email written to {recipient_path}")

# Write to sender sent folder
sender_path = os.path.join(TESTBED, "emails", sender, eml_filename)
with open(sender_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(eml_content)
print(f"COPY: Email copied to {sender_path}")

# Verify by reading back
with open(recipient_path, "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
print(f"VERIFY: File exists and has {len(content)} bytes")
print("---EMAIL CONTENT---")
print(content)
print("---END---")
'''
